1610 → 1756: what changed Dundovic-1610-Zadar-Census Stanojevic-1756-Zadar-Census



































16101756Households80132Souls431820Mean household5.46.2Distinct surnames5171Surnames in both—8
Biograd grows from 80 households to 132 and from 431 souls to 820, but only 8 of 51 surnames survive the gap — the lowest continuity rate of the four. Tomić expands from 2 households to 6 and Bilić from 1 to 3; Veličić and Lukačić shrink. Biograd was sacked and largely emptied during the Morean War, and the 1756 roster reads as a substantially new population.
In both censuses (8): Tomić 2→6, Drašković 2→5, Matković 3→2, Bilić 1→3, Veličić 3→1, Lukačić 2→1, Jelić 1→1, Šodić 1→1.
In 1610, gone by 1756 (43): Ajazović, Babić, Bubić, Bubičić, Bubovčević, Buljefčić, Cingano, Dabanović, Divić, Dlančić, Dragin, Dražisić, Gilasov, Halužić, Hoda, Ivković, Jeličić, Jurasović, Kagić, Kolarović, Komić, Kozlica, Majić, Majuzić, Maratov, Miletić, Moresinov, Morlak, Nagermica, Ostojić, Paroco, Pehrinović, Piližarić, Radasinova, Radašinović, Stulić, Vitanović, Vukmanović, Zmajčić, Zojić, da Sale, Škropeta.
New in 1756 (63): Spadić, Tolić, Žabetić, Buljevac, Dobanović, Gašparović, Grzić, Jelčić, Mrvić, Mršun, Pelizarić, Stampalia, Zečan, Doljanac, Grzan, Jukić, Juričić, Kolar, Lalin, Lukacina, Mažanović, Mikuličić, Miošević, Morosini, Plaćar, Punoš, Rudić, Strpić, Vulelja, Šimičić, Bošković, Doliba, Galić, Grujičić, Ješkina, Jurešić, Kašić, Kurt, Marat, Matošić, Milošić, Mrvica, Pančić, Pilatović, Pletikosa, Pribilović, Saja, Savin, Smajčić, Sokol, Tomaš, Torlak, Tulić, Velić, Vidović, Vujašin, Vukov, Vulinović, Vušković, Zorić, Zulin, Škilić, Žabar.
Likely the same family, split by spelling

1610 Jeličić (2, Gelicich) ~ 1756 Jelčić (3, Gelicich) — The two ingests normalized the identical Venetian string Gelicich differently — Jeličić in 1610, Jelčić in 1756. Same name, same town; a normalization artifact, not a population change.
1610 Pilizarić (4, Pilizarich) ~ 1756 Pelizarić (3, Pelizarich)
1610 Dabanović (1, Dabanouich) ~ 1756 Dobanović (3, Dobanovich)
1610 Zmajčić (1, Smaicich) ~ 1756 Smajčić (1, Smaicich) — Again the identical Venetian string Smaicich, normalized two ways.
1610 Maratov (1, Maratou) ~ 1756 Marat (1, Marat)

These are flagged, not merged — merging Person or Surname pages needs a decision.
(Two classes of split have since been reconciled and no longer show up as turnover here: hub files that carried two canonical spellings — Sodić/Šodić, Vicinović/Vičinović, Drasković/Drašković, Kuzinović/Kužinović, Barbarosa/Barbarossa — and the former Smoljić hub, merged into Smolić on 2026-09-08 as one family.)
A surname that became a byname
Vitanović is one of the larger Biograd families in 1610 — 5 households. It is absent from the 1756 surname list, but it survives in the survey as a byname: Toma Mersun detto Vitanovich and Sime Mersun detto Vitanovich in Biograd, Toma Mersum detto Vitanovich in Vrana, and Misco Zorich detto Vitanovich in Biograd Stanojevic-1756-Zadar-Census. The line did not disappear; it was absorbed into the Mršun and Zorić households and demoted to a distinguishing epithet. This is the one demonstrable 1610→1756 family link in the village, and it is invisible if you compare surname lists alone.
How much of this turnover is real?
Some of it is certainly an artifact. The two censuses were written by different scribes 146 years apart, and their Venetian spellings were normalized into Croatian by two separate ingests using different judgement — so one family can enter the wiki under two hubs and read as a disappearance plus an arrival. The pairs listed above are the visible cases; there are probably more that no longer look similar enough to spot. Treat the continuity figures as a lower bound.
The rest is real, and has a cause: the Morean War (1684–1699) and the Venetian resettlement that followed it moved large numbers of people into the Zadar contado from Ottoman territory. Both effects push in the same direction, which is why the raw overlap is so low.

Bjelaj (Bilaj)
Main castle in Lika; in Turkish times provided 100 cavalry + 200 foot Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Ilija Janković’s June 1687 raid (800 men, 400 cavalry; killed Bilaj captain’s brother and son, doc 170). Conquered by Venetians c. 1692; population of ~5000 led to Venetian devotion 1692; tower of disdar stormed by Juka Vukmirović with bombs. 5000 souls migration with conti Đurić, Pirić, Zorić, settled Plavno, Zrmanja, Pađene, Mokro-Polje, Oton (1692-03-21). Sunaje village near Bilaj — Milovan Babić (doc 215). Christians from Bilaj area used Zarvovizza/Zrvnica mountains to ambush Turks Dec 1687.

places/Bjeline.title: Bjeline
places/Bjeline.content:
Bjeline
Village east of Benkovac. 1528: mezra “Stare Biline” with 2 non-Muslim houses, where Culina-sin-Milica-b????-Bjeline (knez, timar in Lika) resided Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. 1540: home of two “popovski sinovi” Nikola and Josif (Jusuf) — possible glagoljaški priest’s family. Old Catholic church Sv. Ivan (today orthodox Sv. Petka).
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Bjeline / Bigliane (under Nadin pertinenza 1689) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Zaviša Janković’s holdings — 20 (later 40) ploughing oxen (docs 329, 330, 377). Note: Bilisani (Belissane / Nabelissane near Obrovac) is a distinct village despite similar name.

places/Blagaj.title: Blagaj
places/Blagaj.content:
Blagaj
Old fortress above the Buna spring; medieval seat of the Bosnian rulers, then of oblasni gospodari Sandalj Hranić and herceg Stjepan Vukčić Kosača (after whom Humska zemlja was renamed Hercegovina from 1448). After Ottoman conquest, seat of the nahija Blagaj in Sandzak-Hercegovina.
In Bosnian-Franciscan literary tradition, Buna under Blagaj came to function as a symbolic origin point of Hercegovina (“Blagaj šeher, a kasaba Mostar” — old proverb). Šarić: this symbolic charge underpins the constructed Buna-river origin legend of the Bunjevci, deployed by the Bosanska franjevačka provincija in 16th–17th-c. jurisdictional disputes with Dalmatian dioceses Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

places/Blato.title: Blato
places/Blato.content:
Blato (Hercegovina)
Hercegovina/Mostar-area province from which 5000 souls migrated 1694 (with Brochno, Goranci) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Also a village in Mostar district where Rašić had property.

places/Bocagnazzo.title: Bocagnazzo
places/Bocagnazzo.content:
Bocagnazzo (Bokanjac)
Venetian/Italian name for the village of Bokanjac near Zadar. In 1672 promised as a settlement site to harambaša Šimun Milković for 25 families (doc. 200) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Notes
Same place as the existing Bokanjac page.

places/Bogoselci.title: Bogoselci
places/Bogoselci.content:
Bogoselci
Village near Zadar; its inhabitants, with those of Bibinje, Kolarin, Brkljača and Sukošan, were posted at the Margitina Voda pass-guard under harambaša Ivan Dević (1663, doc. 130) Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I.
People associated with this place

Ivan Dević (see Devic)

places/Boka.title: Boka
places/Boka.content:
Boka Kotorska
Gulf of Kotor on the Adriatic. Monsignor Laližić served as exarch and vicegerent of the Patriarch of Peć in Boka (granted a stipend 1695, doc. 280) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Bokanjac.title: Bokanjac
places/Bokanjac.content:
Bokanjac
Village in Julio Soppe’s sub-region (doc 19); under Zemunik pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
1610 census (Museo Correr) Dundovic-1610-Zadar-Census

places/Boraja.title: Boraja
places/Boraja.content:
Boraja
Village in the Šibenik hinterland; subject of an uskakanje petition in 1683 by harambaša Vid Bačić and alfier Petar Radić (doc. 332) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Borajna.title: Borajna
places/Borajna.content:
Borajna
W. Hercegovina locality near the eastern edge of Bekija; 1477 Hercegovina defter winter pasture of the Krmpote katun (with Buhovo, Ledinac, Veseli-Vstak) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

places/Boricevac.title: Boricevac
places/Boricevac.content:
Boričevac
Village in Lika / Bosanska Krajina border, mentioned in Desnica II Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Bosanska-Krajina.title: Bosanska-Krajina
places/Bosanska-Krajina.content:
Bosanska krajina
NW-Bosnian frontier with Habsburg Croatia. Šarić distinguishes two zapadnobosanski Bunjevac groups Saric-2008-Bunjevci:

“Stariji” — around Livno, Kupres, Glamoc (continuous from 16th c.).
“Noviji” — Bosanski Petrovac, Ključ, Sanski Most. These are actually lički Bunjevci who settled after the 1878 Austro-Hungarian occupation: predominantly Krnjeuša, Kolunić (Bosanski Petrovac), Velagići, Ramići (Ključ), Kljevci (Sanski Most). Many of these settlements were destroyed/displaced in WWII and the 1992–95 war.

The “stariji” component witnesses Catholic Vlach continuity in the prekoplaninska imigracijska zona of Sandzak-Klis; the 1743 vizitacija in Gornje Glamocko-Polje registers Catholic “Matheus Bunievza” as one such trace.

places/Bosna.title: Bosna
places/Bosna.content:
Bosna (Bosnia)
Ottoman frontier province bordering Venetian Dalmatia; home region of Ottoman raiders such as the četobaša Karalija, active from Livno Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Brac.title: Brac
places/Brac.content:
Brač
Adriatic island (doc 55) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Cornaro’s galley off Brač (doc 172).

places/Brdar.title: Brdar
places/Brdar.content:
Brdar
Locality recorded as the seat/origin of a Prejić lineage branch in the region of the Vlasi Istre (attested 1540) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.
People associated with this place

Prejic-sin-Matijasa-b????-Brdar

places/Brgud.title: Brgud
places/Brgud.content:
Brgud (kod Benkovca)
Village in Bukovica. 1528–1530: 15 non-Muslim houses; home of Samil-Jakovic-b????-Brgud (recorded in 1530 sumarni after conversion to Islam, absent from earlier mufassal) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. 1540 register: 16 non-Muslim houses. Old Catholic church on site of today’s orthodox Sv. Lazar.

places/Bribir.title: Bribir
places/Bribir.content:
Bribir
Castle, on confine with Zadar (docs 19, 51, 315) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Mikiel’s Knin tour 1685 included castle assessment.

places/Brochno.title: Brochno
places/Brochno.content:
Broćno
Hercegovina province from which 5000 souls migrated 1694 (with Blato, Goranci) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II; settled at Zadvarje and Vrgorac.

places/Brod.title: Brod
places/Brod.content:
Slavonski Brod
Sava crossing where Imperial army crossed 1688 (doc 211) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Imperial victory at Brod / crossing of Sava early Aug 1688 — Bosnian pasha defeated.

places/Bruska.title: Bruska
places/Bruska.content:
Bruška
Village NE of Benkovac. 1528: 7 non-Muslim houses. 1540: 6 non-Muslim houses — the only village remaining in vlach nahija Bukovica after the 1538 mass defection Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

places/Bruvno.title: Bruvno
places/Bruvno.content:
Bruvno
Village in Lika Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 365). Conte Obradović from there. Vid Petrović killed at Bruvno 1707 by Canagetti.

places/Bubnjane.title: Bubnjane
places/Bubnjane.content:
Bubnjane
Locality near Tinj and Lišani; part of the 400-kanapa investitura granted to col. Vuk Crnica by Barbaro in 1671 (doc. 182) Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I.

places/Buda.title: Buda
places/Buda.content:
Buda / Budapest
Ottoman Buda eyalet capital until 1686 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 62). Captured Turkish caravan story (doc 62). Atlagić served at the siege of Buda (doc 217).

places/Budimski-Ejalet.title: Budimski-Ejalet
places/Budimski-Ejalet.content:
Budimski ejalet
Largest Ottoman administrative province of Hungary (Buda eyalet), 1541–1686. Comprised Sandzak-Mohac (Baranja), Backa, and other northern districts.
Receiver of two demographic waves relevant to Bunjevac history Saric-2008-Bunjevci:

1530s+ — Ottoman deportations of “buntovni vlaški element” from Vilajet-Hrvati.
1606+ — main Bunjevac wave from Sandzak-Klis / Sandzak-Krka after the Drniš revolt and other Klis-area unrest, settling the bajska/somborska/subotička nahija depopulated after the 1598 Pálffy migrations.

places/Budin.title: Budin
places/Budin.content:
Budin
Place where Sinobad-Vukčević-Mitrović Morlachs lived (doc 19, 30) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Under Islam pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga. Some families left Budin because of Sinobad-Mitrović feud 1684; Polo Michiel asked to mediate.

places/Budva.title: Budva
places/Budva.content:
Budva
Adriatic port “aperta e con poca difesa” — threatened by Skadar Sandžak May 1685 (doc 72) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Levant career station of Ottaviano Lazzari (doc 345).

places/Buhovo.title: Buhovo
places/Buhovo.content:
Buhovo
Western Hercegovina locality near today’s eastern edge of Bekija. Recorded in the 1477 Hercegovina defter as a winter pasture (zimište) of the Krmpote katun (alongside Borajna, Ledinac, Veseli-Vstak) — about 22 km west of the Buna river Saric-2008-Bunjevci (Aličić 1985:130–131).

places/Bukovica.title: Bukovica
places/Bukovica.content:
Bukovica
Karst region in northern Dalmatia between Zadar, Knin, and Velebit. Core settlement area of the Vlasi-Istre in the 16th c. Forms an Ottoman nahija in the 1528–1530 register (60 houses, 11 villages); reduced to a single village (Bruška) by 1540 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Later receives Hercegovinian Catholic Vlachs (Bunjevci) and Orthodox Vlach migrants.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Central focus throughout Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II; tax/herd zone. Smiljanić family origin. Pasha’s incursion April 1688 plundered it. Villages of Krmpote-Bukovica, Parčić, Modrino-Selo, Erveničani. Under Novigrad pertinenza 1689 Cornaro Liga (with Karin, two Obrovci, Krusevo, Žegar, Ervenik, Zelengrad, Drinjci, Otavac, Popovici, Lussichi). 1704 Bukovica Revolt (Pop Petar Jagodić-Kuridža Uprising).

places/Buna.title: Buna
places/Buna.content:
Buna (river and place)
Short (~8 km) right-bank tributary of the Neretva in W. Hercegovina, rising at a karst spring beneath the old fortress of Blagaj. Place “Buna” stands on the river of the same name.
Significance for genealogy
Center of the Buna-river origin legend of the Bunjevci, first written down by Alberto Fortis (1778, Lika) and fra Marijan Lanosović (1794, Bačka). Šarić argues the legend is a 17th-c. Bosnian-Franciscan construct — using the Buna and Blagaj (medieval seat of Sandalj Hranić and Stjepan Vukčić Kosača) to symbolically anchor Bosnian Franciscan jurisdictional claims over Bunjevac populations against rival Dalmatian dioceses.
The 1477 Hercegovina defter for nahija Blagaj (which contained Buna) shows a different picture: among 36 vlach džemats, none can be identified as Bunjevac. The dominant figure is vojvoda Petar Hrabren (Donji Vlasi, manastirski ktitor), suggesting a predominantly Orthodox vlach population. The Neretva already in the 15th c. divided ikavski (W) from ijekavski (E) štokavski; the consistently-ikavski Bunjevci therefore cannot have originated east of the river Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
The closest core Bunjevac winter pastures (Krmpote zimišta Buhovo, Borajna) lay 22 km west by air; selo Vojnici-Ljubuski 35 km west.

places/Buncici.title: Buncici
places/Buncici.content:
Bunčići
Village in Radmilović-Dubrava near Bileća, Hercegovina. Site of a tall medieval stećak with Cyrillic inscription naming Bunac-Rusovic-b????-Buncici — likely a vlach starešina from the Banjani Vlach aglomeracija (Bešlagić 1971:390) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Connected to the medieval Bun-stem Vlachs (Vukota-Buncic-b1419 in the 1419 katun documents).

places/Bunjane.title: Bunjane
places/Bunjane.content:
Bunjane (Đakovica)
Village near Đakovica in Metohija; 1330 Dečanska povelja records 62 houses of agricultural (Serbian) population Saric-2008-Bunjevci. The toponym belongs to the medieval Bun-stem onomastic family of place- and clan-names (with Tudoricevci / Bunovići, Bunuševci of Vranjsko-Krajiste, Bunčići of Buncici).

places/Bunusa.title: Bunusa
places/Bunusa.content:
Bunuša
Village south of Leskovac. Toponymic relic of the medieval Vlasi Bunuševci of Vranjsko-Krajiste; result of territorialization of their katun Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

places/Burgenland-Vlahija.title: Burgenland-Vlahija
places/Burgenland-Vlahija.content:
Burgenland Vlahija
Cluster of 12 Vlach-settled villages on the slopes of Kiseg gorje in southern Burgenland, on Batthyány and Erdődy estates Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. First mention 1541; settlement likely between 1517 and 1541 (perhaps c. 1538). Inhabitants were “libertini” (free peasants in military service); old Štokavian-Ikavian Croatian speakers, Catholic. Possibly drawn from same Vlach pool as the Vlasi-Istre migration cycle.

places/Buzet.title: Buzet
places/Buzet.content:
Buzet
Town in northern Venetian Istria. Buzetski Kras was a refuge for the Poropat kindred c. 1518–1528 before their return to Zrmanja Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Long-term concentration of Poropat (Poropatići) on the Venetian side at Trstenik, Dane, Lanišće.

places/Carigrad.title: Carigrad
places/Carigrad.content:
Carigrad / Istanbul
Ottoman capital (docs 53, 65) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. One Radoš brother held captive here 1685.

places/Castel-Venier.title: Castel-Venier
places/Castel-Venier.content:
Castel Venier (Vinjerac)
Venetian coastal fort in the Posedarje area, associated with the Boljac Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Notes
Corresponds to the town of Vinjerac.

places/Cattaro.title: Cattaro
places/Cattaro.content:
Cattaro (Kotor)
Venetian/Italian name for Kotor. Antonio Zen served as provveditor estraordinario at Cattaro in 1686 (doc. 131) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Notes
Same place as the existing Kotor page.

places/Cazin.title: Cazin
places/Cazin.content:
Cazin
Lika fortress (Bosanska Krajina), 150 horse + 300 foot Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Ceranje.content:
Ceranje

places/Cetina.title: Cetina
places/Cetina.content:
Cetina
River and surrounding region. Forms the southeastern boundary of Vilajet-Hrvati. Site of the 1516 Ottoman capture of utvrda Nutjak, after which 9 vlach džemata defected from Poljica to Ottoman territory in Radobilja Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Cetinski Morlaci recorded by Domenico Negri (c. 1500) as speakers of “iskvarenim latinskim jezikom” — “Romani”.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Cetina campaign March–April 1685 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (docs 28, 33, 42, 55, 59–61). Cetina Morlak migration March 1685: Ilija Peraica brought 600 armed men + families + 30,000 small animals + 10,000 cattle to Trogir territory. Atlagić retreated across Cetina April 1687; pasha at sorgente di Cettina April 1688. Cetinski-Most (Cetinski most / ponte di Cettina) — bridge mentioned docs 56, 59, 60. Vukovićev most / “ponte Vucovich” — docs 59, 61. Otok — island in Cetina where Turks camped before Sinj battle. Dragović — peninsula on Cetina with Greek-rite monastery, restored by Bušović 1694.

places/Cetinje.title: Cetinje
places/Cetinje.content:
Cetinje
Patriarch of Peć’s planned new seat 1686, with intent to send 100 cavalry to Janković (doc 160) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Seat of vladika Visarion Borilović. Bishopric of Cetinje 1707 (doc 366).

places/Cetinski-Most.title: Cetinski-Most
places/Cetinski-Most.content:
Cetinski most
Bridge over Cetina (docs 56, 59, 60) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Vukovićev most / “ponte Vucovich” also on Cetina (docs 59, 61).

places/Cherso.title: Cherso
places/Cherso.content:
Cherso (Cres)
Venetian/Italian name for the Kvarner island of Cres. Padron Francesco Pokupić captained a tartana from Cherso (1696, doc. 290) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Notes
Same place as the existing Cres page.

places/Cicarija.title: Cicarija
places/Cicarija.content:
Ćićarija
Karst highland region between Habsburska-Istra and Mletacka-Istra, home to the bilingual Slavic-Romance “Ćići” Vlachs. Last preserved area of the Istro-Romanian / “vlaški” idiom, today only in Zejane and a handful of villages along Čepić polje Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

places/Cipici.title: Cipici
places/Cipici.content:
Čipići
Sub-village of Petropolje, seat of the Gargić-Čipić (see Cipic) knez sub-line; conte Giacomo Gargić detto Cipich named as its conte in 1647 (doc. 18) Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I.

places/Citluk-Licki.title: Citluk-Licki
places/Citluk-Licki.content:
Čitluk Lički
Village near Novi in Lika Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Origin of Vukašin Rošić’s 20 families (doc 45) and Vuko Vojkorsić’s family (doc 54).

places/Citluk.title: Citluk
places/Citluk.content:
Čitluk
Village of Petropolje; Marko Omeljić “da Čitluk” signed the Petropolje uskakanje contract in 1647 (doc. 18) Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I.
Notes
Distinct from Citluk-Licki in Lika.

places/Cliuno.title: Cliuno
places/Cliuno.content:
Cliuno (Livno)
Venetian/Latin name for Livno in western Bosnia. Site of Janković’s and Smiljanić’s raids of 1686; after the second Livno raid (doc. 141) the Ottoman relief force under a new Zvornik pasha and the alajbeg Filipović was routed Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Notes
Same place as the existing Livno page.

places/Cres.title: Cres
places/Cres.content:
Cres
Adriatic island; Pokupić’s tartana from there Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Crete.title: Crete
places/Crete.content:
Crete
Mediterranean island; the principal theatre and casus belli of the Candian-War-1645-1669, fought between Venice and the Ottoman Empire over Venetian Candia. The war’s Dalmatian front drove the Morlach/Bunjevac migrations central to this wiki. Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I
People associated with this place

(none directly; referenced via the Candian War)

places/Crna-Gora.title: Crna-Gora
places/Crna-Gora.content:
Crna Gora (Montenegro)
Region; parts joined Sandžak-beg of Skadar against Venetians 1685 (doc 72) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Crno.title: Crno
places/Crno.content:
Crno (Karno)
Village in Smiljanić sub-region (doc 19, 51); under Zemunik pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Crnomelj.title: Crnomelj
places/Crnomelj.content:
Črnomelj
Town in Bela Krajina, southern Kranjska. Nearby Marindol was a settlement of Vlach uskok refugees from 1551 (register names Stanoje Prijić as desetnik) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

places/Cucullovaci.title: Cucullovaci
places/Cucullovaci.content:
Čučulovci
Village of origin of the Miljanić (harambaša Petar Miljanić), whose people resettled in Vrsi Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I.
Notes
Also spelled Cuculovaci.

places/Cuculovaci.title: Cuculovaci
places/Cuculovaci.content:
Čučulovci
Village of origin of Petar Miljanić’s band; recorded (as resettled in Vrsi, 70 → 6 fighters) in the muster around the Battle of Ribnik, 1648 Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I.
Notes
Variant spelling of Cucullovaci.

places/Cvrsnica.title: Cvrsnica
places/Cvrsnica.content:
Čvrsnica
Mountain in W. Hercegovina; 1477 summer pasture (ljetište) of the Krmpote katun (with Vran and Ljubusa) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

places/Cyclut.title: Cyclut
places/Cyclut.content:
Čitluk (Hercegovina, near Mostar)
Ottoman fortress/town in Hercegovina near Mostar; defended in Morean War (first and second defense) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 358). Sinobad and Zaviša fought there. Distinct from Citluk-Licki (in Lika).

places/Dalmatia.title: Dalmatia
places/Dalmatia.content:
Dalmatia (Dalmacija)
Adriatic coastal region under Venetian rule in the Uskok period; theatre of the Ottoman–Venetian frontier wars and of settlement of Vlach/Morlach uskoks. Numerous Venetian-service families are attested here Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Notes
For the specifically Venetian administrative unit see also Mletacka-Dalmacija.

places/Dicmo.title: Dicmo
places/Dicmo.content:
Dicmo
Vallone near Sinj; Ali camped here April 1687 (doc 169); later place where settlers from Duvno + Rama placed; Orthodox enclave (docs 169, 184) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Diklo.title: Diklo
places/Diklo.content:
Diklo
Village in Julio Soppe’s sub-region (doc 19); under Lower Kotari (Milković serdarstvo) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Djevrske.title: Djevrske
places/Djevrske.content:
Đevrske
Village in the Bukovica; origin of uskoci who resettled near Petrčane. Harambaša Smoljan Miković led men “iz Đevrsaka” at Ribnik, 1648 (doc. 39) Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I.

places/Dobra-Voda.title: Dobra-Voda
places/Dobra-Voda.content:
Dobra Voda
Village under Ostrovica pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Dobropoglie.title: Dobropoglie
places/Dobropoglie.content:
Dobropolje
Village listed under the Ostrovica pertinenza in the 1689 Cornaro Liga Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Dobropoljci.title: Dobropoljci
places/Dobropoljci.content:
Dobropoljci
Origin village of uskoci resettled at Ljubač in 1648; Jovan Dobrić led a party from here Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I.

places/Dobruca-Vas.title: Dobruca-Vas
places/Dobruca-Vas.content:
Dobruča Vas (Dobrudža)
Village near Benkovac. 1528: 7 non-Muslim houses, residence of Petar-Najcinovic-b????-Dobruca-Vas (knez, head of Benković dzemat) and his relative Nenad-Jancic-b????-Dobruca-Vas Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. 1574 vakuf register: 15 Christian houses on Husrev-beg vakuf. Najčinović returned here after 1540 (1533 Zadar grain contract).

places/Donja-Jagodnja.content:
Donja Jagodnja
Village of the Zadar contado, enumerated in the 1756 Grimani land-and-souls survey as Giagogne Inferior Stanojevic-1756-Zadar-Census.

places/Donje-Biljane.content:
Donje Biljane
Village of the Zadar contado, enumerated in the 1756 Grimani land-and-souls survey as Bigliane Inferior Stanojevic-1756-Zadar-Census.

places/Dracevac-Zadarski.content:

places/Dracevac.title: Dracevac
places/Dracevac.content:
Dračevac (kod Jasenica)
Village in nahija near Jasenice. 1590: residence of Hasan-aga-Frletic-b????-Dracevac, Muslim convert and Venetian informant on the Novigrad-more frontier; also the home of the father of uskok Andrija-Frletic-b????-Dracevac Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

Not to be confused with Dračevac Zadarski (Malpaga), a separate village of the Zadar littoral covered by the 1610 census.

places/Dragomirani.title: Dragomirani
places/Dragomirani.content:
Dragomirani
Settlement in Donji Karin area (today only the toponym Dragomirov bunar survives). 1528: 2 non-Muslim houses; 1540: 4 non-Muslim houses including pop Stipan Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

places/Dragovic.title: Dragovic
places/Dragovic.content:
Dragović
Peninsula on Cetina with old monastery, restored by Bušović 1694 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 317). Calogeri di Dragovich; granted lands at Međupuće (50 kanapa).

places/Drnis.title: Drnis
places/Drnis.content:
Drniš
Town in Petrovo polje, Sandzak-Klis. Site of the 1608 Drniš revolt of muslim and Vlach population under drniški aga Mehmed-Terzibasic-b????-Drnis — its suppression triggered the transfer of 2,000 morlach houses across the Danube reported by the Šibenik knez to the Venetian Senate Saric-2008-Bunjevci (see Bunjevac-Migration-to-Backa-c1606).
Drniš/Petrovo polje was one of the documented emigration sources for Bunjevac flight to Bačka, alongside Vrlika and Livno.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Captured/contested area; staging point March 1685 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 51). Fenzi the governor; threatened multiple times; Selman pasha’s defeat here; 200 men from Šibenik to garrison. Tomaso Zavoreo governator (doc 314). Petrovo-Polje near Drniš. Petrova Crkva (Petrovo Crichva) — church near Drniš/Petrovo polje (doc 195).

places/Drvenik.title: Drvenik
places/Drvenik.content:
Drvenik
Origin place of uskoci resettled near Nin; Martin Tomičić led a party from here (Ribnik, 1648) Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I.

places/Dugopolje.title: Dugopolje
places/Dugopolje.content:
Dugopolje
Village near Klis where frate Andrea hid 1687 (doc 182) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Duvno.title: Duvno
places/Duvno.content:
Duvno (Tomislavgrad)
Hercegovina town/region, scene of the 23 Aug 1687 raid where Stojan Janković was killed by musket and sword while only 8–10 companions followed (doc 174) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Zeno burned the mosque-fortress.

places/Erdelja.title: Erdelja
places/Erdelja.content:
Erdelja (Prikanci)
Vlach settlement on the Bosiljevsko vlastelinstvo of the Frankapan. Founded c. 1540s by a smaller Vlach group in libertini service to grof Frankapan Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Catholic / pokatoličeni Vlachs.

places/Ervenicani.title: Ervenicani
places/Ervenicani.content:
Erveničani
Village in Bukovica, possibly variant of Ervenik Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Ervenik.title: Ervenik
places/Ervenik.content:
Ervenik
Village in nahija Zrmanja. 1528: 5 non-Muslim houses (recorded as “Irvnenik”). 1540: residence of pop Radoje (one of two priests recorded among Vlasi Istre that year) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Old Catholic churches Sv. Mihovil and Sv. Nikola.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Under Novigrad pertinenza (Hrvenik) in 1689 Cornaro Liga Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (docs 329, 330, 377). Settled with Bjelajci 1692. Zaviša Janković’s holdings; Novac Vujanić captain 1704.

places/Esseco.title: Esseco
places/Esseco.content:
Osijek
Slavonian town. Vizier sent Hercegovina alaibeg from Osijek 1687 (doc 174 footnote) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Filipjakov.title: Filipjakov
places/Filipjakov.content:
Sveti Filip i Jakov
Coastal settlement in the Zadar/Šibenik area associated with uskok families in Desnica I Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I.

places/Forte-Opus.title: Forte-Opus
places/Forte-Opus.content:
Forte Opus / Opuzen
Venetian fort near Neretva mouth, with malarial garrison (doc 213) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Mentioned doc 55 as Opuzen / Opus.

places/Glamoc-Polje.title: Glamoc-Polje
places/Glamoc-Polje.content:
Glamočko polje
Field by Glamoč in western Bosnia; site where Jovan Sinobad was killed in a clash with Ottomans in 1715 (doc. 372) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
Notes

Likely the same locality as Glamocko-Polje (variant link spelling).

places/Glamoc.title: Glamoc
places/Glamoc.content:
Glamoč
Town and district in western Bosnia. 1524 Habsburg border reports described a “dangerous settlement of 6,000 vlach houses” at Glamoč and Unac, an origin point for raiding into Habsburg Croatia (Vasić 1963) Saric-2008-Bunjevci. Alajbeg Filipović’s palaces here were burned in the Glamoč–Grahovo campaign of August 1684 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Glamocko-Polje.title: Glamocko-Polje
places/Glamocko-Polje.content:
Glamočko polje
SW Bosnian polje. 1524 Habsburg border reports describe a “dangerous settlement of 6,000 vlach houses” in Glamoc and Unac — origin point for raiding into Habsburg Croatia and Kranjska (Vasić 1963) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
In 1743 a biskupska vizitacija of Gornji Glamoč registered a Catholic named “Matheus Bunievza” — late Bunjevac trace in the prekoplaninska imigracijska zona Saric-2008-Bunjevci (Erdeljanović 1930).
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Glamoč–Grahovo Campaign (Aug 1684): 5000 Morlachs under Janković, Smiljanić, Bortulačić raided Glamoč; alajbeg Filipović’s palaces burned, 50 Turks killed Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II; on return, ambushed two Bosnian-Hercegovinian pashas at Grahovo. Burgo of Glamoč burned by Zaviša after Cuprez (1696 attestation). Site of Sinobad’s death 1715 (doc 372): Andrija/Jovan Sinobad killed there. Filipović came from here.

places/Gorica.title: Gorica
places/Gorica.content:
Gorica (Tinj)
Catholic Vlach Bunjevac village in the Vojnić-Tinj corridor. Pre-1647 was within Sandžak Klis, kadiluk of Halil-beg of Vrana. Pop don Stjepan Sorić was župnik here from at least 1636 (per Šarić 2024/2008).
Source-village of major uskakanje

1647-05-29 — knez Frano Posedarski receives Cordo, Filipac and other Goričani who have crossed; Foscolo writes to receive them (doc. 5 Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I).
1647-06-17 — Foscolo’s proclama protects “Morlacchi da Gorizza, Percos et altri luoghi circonvicini venuti alla devotione del prencipe” (doc. 12).
1647 onward — don Stjepan Sorić of Gorica leads the uskakanje of the Goričani Catholic Vlachs into Venetian territory; mass-raids on Udbina (1648); killed at Ribnik 1648-07-17.
1648-07-31 — After Sorić’s death the Goričani elect his brother Mate Sorić as their new capo (doc. 41).

People

Don Stjepan Sorić
Mate Sorić (brother)

places/Grabovac.title: Grabovac
places/Grabovac.content:
Grabovac
Orthodox monastery in Baranja, founded 1585 by monks from manastir Dragović on the Cetina in Sandzak-Klis. Reinforced 1619 by Orthodox Vlachs from Klis-area accompanying further Cetina-region monastics Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Documents the parallel Orthodox migration stream into Podunavlje alongside the Bunjevac (Catholic) wave (see Bunjevac-Migration-to-Backa-c1606).

places/Gracac.content:

places/Grahovo.content:
Bosansko Grahovo
Site of the 26 Aug 1684 Morlak victory: 5000 Morlachs under Janković, Smiljanić, Bortulačić ambushed two Bosnian-Hercegovinian pashas; 150 Turks killed (incl. 30 court aga, 2 “Bugliuch bassé”) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (docs 7, 27, 56). Mazut-paša’s kjehaja killed by Sinovčić (doc 32 footnote). Smiljanić lightly wounded in hand.

places/Grbalj.title: Grbalj
places/Grbalj.content:
Grbalj (Zuppa)
Contado near Kotor at risk 1685 (doc 72) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Gruhe.content:
Gruhe
Village in Julio Soppe’s sub-region (doc 19); under Zemunik pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Grusi.title: Grusi
places/Grusi.content:
Gruši
Settlement in the Zadar hinterland (today part of Zadar); site of the earliest surviving krajiški statut, Grusi-Krajiski-Statut-1654 (5 August 1654) Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I.

places/Habsburska-Istra.title: Habsburska-Istra
places/Habsburska-Istra.content:
Habsburška Istra (Habsburg Istria)
Inland and northeastern Istria under Habsburg rule, including Pazinska-Grofovija and parts of Kras. Refuge for Croatian Vlach migrants c. 1518–1523 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Source area for the 1528 return migration to Ottoman territory and the 1570 Pazin revolt-driven defection.

places/Hadzi-Lukovo.title: Hadzi-Lukovo
places/Hadzi-Lukovo.content:
Hadži Lukovo
Village in Mostar/Zaupa province, given to Rašić Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Hercegnovi.title: Hercegnovi
places/Hercegnovi.content:
Hercegnovi (Castel Novo)
Bay-of-Kotor stronghold under Venetian siege 1687–88; captured during the Morean War (doc 175) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Spingaroli participated in the conquest. Vodmac vineyard at Podhumnica region (formerly Resul Aga Babović’s) granted to Bishop Simeon Prešević 1697 (doc 307).

places/Hercegovina.title: Hercegovina
places/Hercegovina.content:
Hercegovina
Region south of Bosnia. Origin point of major Vlach migration streams into 16th-c. Croatia. Renamed “Hercegovina” from Humska zemlja from 1448 (after herceg Stjepan Vukčić Kosača, seat at Blagaj).
1477 defter
The 1477 Ottoman defter records istimâlet contracts with Vlach voivodes Vladimir-vojvoda-b????-Hercegovina (nahija Mostar) and Dadoje-vojvoda-b????-Hercegovina / Sinan-beg Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. The defter shows three core katuns of the future Bunjevac population Saric-2008-Bunjevci:

Krmpote — Vukic-Krmpotic-b????-Hercegovina, nahija Humska zemlja, 11 houses; pastures Buhovo/Borajna/Ledinac/Veseli-Vstak (winter) and Cvrsnica/Vran/Ljubusa (summer).
Vojnići — Vukasin-sin-Vojihne-b????-Mostar, nahija Mostar, 10 houses + 3 unmarried; eponymous selo Vojnici-Ljubuski.
Sladovići — Milosav-sin-Sladica-b????-Mostar, nahija Mostar, 19 houses; villages Podaca/Igrane/Kozica.

In the same defter, nahija Blagaj has 36 vlach džemats (none Bunjevac); the dominant figure is vojvoda Petar-Hrabren-b????-Hercegovina of Donji Vlasi — predominantly Orthodox population around the Buna river.
Migration source area
Source area of later Bunjevac (Catholic) and Orthodox Vlach migrations into Bukovica, Ravni-Kotari, Lika, Backa. Earliest Bun-stem onomastic attestations in the 1477 defter: only Bunjak-sin-Radovana-b????-Rudine (nahija Rudine) and Bunus-sin-Petra-b????-Bjelopavlici (nahija Bjelopavlići) among 7,822 households + their fathers — the romance Bun-stem is already archaic.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Full description by fra Mijo Radonić May 1684 (doc 7) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Ahmed-paša commanded Hercegovina troops at Sinj 1685. Sandžak alaibeg there; Selman pasha threatened Knin (~1696). Brochno-Blato-Goranci migration 1693–1694 (5000 souls) settled at Zadvarje and Vrgorac. Towns/regions enumerated: Trebinje, Stolac, Konjic, Prozor, Počitelj, Gabela, Ljubuški, Mostar, Blagaj, Ranza (Rama), Glamoč, Hliuno (Livno), Sinj, Drniš, Skradin, Knin, Vrlika, Sidraga, Vrana, Obrovac, Grahovo (Bos.), Novi, Nevesinje, Gacko, Imotski, Vrgorac, Makarska, Sandžak Hercegovina (existing).

places/Hreljin.title: Hreljin
places/Hreljin.content:
Hreljin
Zrinski estate in the Croatian coastal hinterland that received the 1605 first Krmpote migration settling at Lic. In 1681 a Dvorska komora inquiry recorded testimony from two Krmpote starešine concerning earlier obligations to the Zrinski family for Lic, Krmpote, and Ledenice residents — Marcus Perpich and Stephanus Duich, both registered as “Rascianus” (a Habsburg administrative attribution, not a self-identification with Serbian ethnicity in the modern sense) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

places/Hum.title: Hum
places/Hum.content:
Hum
Region in Hercegovina claimed as hereditary territory by the Iljanović family Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Hungary.title: Hungary
places/Hungary.content:
Hungary
Ottoman objective for Bosnian troops 1684 (doc 1) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Atlagić’s Hungarian campaign (doc 185). Atlagić had previously held the bassallaggio of Alba Real / Székesfehérvár (doc 217). Rákóczi mission of Baron Vojnović 1706 — Croat noble’s transit through Zadar to Venice/France.

places/Hvar.title: Hvar
places/Hvar.content:
Hvar
Adriatic island (docs 39, 55) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Cornaro went to Hvar; Andrea Longo camerlengo here (docs 193, 217).

places/Igrane.title: Igrane
places/Igrane.content:
Igrane
Village on Biokovo. 1477 Hercegovina defter: “Igre”, part of the Sladović džemat (with Podaca and Kozica) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

places/Imotski.title: Imotski
places/Imotski.content:
Imotski
Hercegovinian-Cetina-frontier fortress (docs 7, 55) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Torre di Varlicca near Imotski destroyed for diversion 1688 (doc 214).

places/Islam.title: Islam
places/Islam.content:
Islam
Village; pertinenza HQ from 1689 Cornaro Liga, including Poličnik, Stošije, Budin, Kašić, Veljani, Suhovare Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Mehmed beg’s name attached to the village. Under Zaviša Mitrović 1691 (doc 309). Captain Ilija Nanić of Kašić & Islam. Mitrović family had houses and 400 gognali there from 1670 (Barbaro investiture). Conflict with Posedarci (docs 311, 312, 329, 330, 358, 359, 377). Note: 70 Žegarski porodice settled at Islam after Sorić’s 1648 raid (per Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I).

places/Italy.title: Italy
places/Italy.content:
Italy
Homeland of the del-Borro family — the marchesato del Borro in Tuscany Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Izsep.title: Izsep
places/Izsep.content:
Izsép
Selo near Marok in Sandzak-Mohac. 1561 defter records “Martin Bunivac” — same individual as the 1554 attestation in Marok (see Marton-Bunavac-b????-Marok) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

places/Jablanac.title: Jablanac
places/Jablanac.content:
Jablanac
Frankopan port; pays datio for sea transit Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. 1649 Diet of Bratislava (Posonia) art. 32 restored Jablanac and Starigrad to Frankopans.

places/Jagodnja.title: Jagodnja
places/Jagodnja.content:
Jagodnja
Village in Ravni-Kotari paired with Miranje as the dzemat of Tomas-Ruzic-b????-Sibenik (1528) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Old Catholic church (now site of orthodox Sv. Simeon).
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Listed in Bortulačić’s sub-region (doc 19) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Two Jagodne (Giagodne) under Vrana pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga.
Cross-reference
The 1756 Grimani survey enumerates the two Jagodnje separately: Gornja Jagodnja (Giagogne Superior) and Donja Jagodnja (Giagogne Inferior), each with its own roster Stanojevic-1756-Zadar-Census. This page remains the collective entry for the pair.

places/Jasenica.title: Jasenica
places/Jasenica.content:
Jasenica
District in Morlakija; before the Candian War the Rukavine were starešine of the Catholic Morlachs here (Forza 1636, cited by Šarić) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

places/Jesenice-Podgorje.title: Jesenice-Podgorje
places/Jesenice-Podgorje.content:
Jesenice (Podgorje)
Village in the Velebit Podgorje; origin of uskoci resettled between Pag and the fortress of Ljubač Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I.

places/Kaloca.title: Kaloca
places/Kaloca.content:
Kalocsa (Kaloča)
Catholic archdiocesan see in southern Hungary. Locus of the first explicit “parochia Bunievczi” (1622), requested by don Simun-Matkovic-b???? of the Congregatio Propaganda Fide Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
In 1581 in the Kaloča area, knez Vranes-Ivanovic-b????-Kaloca with his knežina is recorded — early evidence of a Dinaric vlach presence pre-dating the main Bunjevac wave to Bačka.
In 1870 Ivan-Antunovic-b1815-Backa launched Bunjevačke i šokačke novine from Kaloča.

places/Kamenjane.title: Kamenjane
places/Kamenjane.content:
Kamenjane
Village in the Bukovica associated with uskok families in Desnica I Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I.

places/Kanjiza.title: Kanjiza
places/Kanjiza.content:
Kanjiža
“Five long days into Bosnia”; Kotarci raided here April 1688 — 300 men under Kalinić from Korlat; took 50 captives, 4000 small animals, 500 large; defeated by Dukajtar’s 100 cavalry; 15-20 dead (doc 202) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Likely Bosanska Kanjiža/Kanjiža in Slavonia or Hungarian Kanjiža.

places/Karin.title: Karin
places/Karin.content:
Karin
Ottoman fortress and Vlach nahija (53 houses, 9 villages) in 1528–1530, headed by vojvoda Zakman-Gledjevac-b????-Karin Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Held a Franciscan monastery (Bezgrešnoga začeća BDM) tending Catholic Vlachs under Ottoman rule until c. 1538; reopened 1550 by Mato-iz-Kresevo-b???? from Visovac. Karin nahija retained territorial integrity through 1540 register (29 houses).
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Hajra/Kosa Lakić’s birthplace (doc 56) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Land dispute with Novigrad (doc 15). Defended itself against pasha April 1688 (doc 198). Mills leased; under Novigrad pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga; mentioned in Obrovac confine 1696. Component of pertinenza.

places/Karlobag.title: Karlobag
places/Karlobag.content:
Karlobag
Adriatic coastal town under Velebit. Habsburg fortress rebuilt 1574, becoming a new flashpoint between the three powers Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Receiving area for Rudelic families relocating from Radovin in 1683.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
“Carlobago, ancient Scrisia” — fortress on Adriatic; 200 archibuggieri 1690, palace built; salt scale opened 1696 to compete with Obrovac Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Imperial subjects retreated here 1687 toward Senj (doc 186). Senj statute confine extends to Lukovo (10 Italian miles south). Karlobag people in encroachment dispute with Tribanj (2 miles from Starigrad). 1592 Senj uskoks raided Karlobag/Pago → Venetian capture; 1615 Senj/Uskok War: Venetians destroyed Karlobag.

places/Karlovac.title: Karlovac
places/Karlovac.content:
Karlovac
Habsburg general’s seat; Erbestein’s command Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Imperial reconquest of Lika and Krbava launched from here 1689. Location of Vojnović feud, 1706 (doc 362).

places/Kasic.title: Kasic
places/Kasic.content:
Kašić
Village under Islam pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (docs 309, 370, 377). Ilija Nanić captain of Kašić & Islam. Gvozden Radasović had property there.

places/Kastela.title: Kastela
places/Kastela.content:
Kaštela
Coastal villages between Trogir and Split. 7 April 1685: 3000 Turkish cavalry under Ahmed-paša of Hercegovina attacked Kaštela; defeated by 3000 castellani + Morlachs; Mustafa Jasko captured (docs 56, 62) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Kaštelani also raided Mostar district 1687.

places/Kistanje.title: Kistanje
places/Kistanje.content:
Kistanje
Village in Bukovica under Ostrovica pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (docs 317, 377). Radin Bunar area near Kistanje.

places/Klicevac.title: Klicevac
places/Klicevac.content:
Kličevac
Ottoman Vlach nahija (16 villages, 120 houses) in 1528–1530 — the largest by households. Included villages Miranje, Jagodnja, headed by Tomas-Ruzic-b????-Sibenik (26 houses) and Radič (123 houses) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Dissolved by 1540, villages absorbed into Kozulova-Polje vakuf.

places/Klis.title: Klis
places/Klis.content:
Klis
Croatian fortress above Split, last major Croatian stronghold south of Velebit until taken by Ottomans in 1537. Gives name to the Sandzak-Klis; first sanjakbeg Murat-beg-Gajdic-b????-Sibenik Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Tomas-Ruzic-b????-Sibenik served here as a soldier before his 1518 flight to Istria.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Fortress; sub-region for various ops Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (docs 38, 42, 51, 60, 61). Cornaro’s camp April 1687.

places/Klisa-Una.title: Klisa-Una
places/Klisa-Una.content:
Klisa (kraj Une)
Town near Una river, Ripac area; raided by Morlachs Holy Thursday April 1688 (doc 201) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Kloster.title: Kloster
places/Kloster.content:
Klošter
Village in Alberti’s sub-region (doc 19) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Knin.title: Knin
places/Knin.content:
Knin
Strategic Croatian fortress town. Pre-Ottoman seat of the Knin diocese (reduced to titular see after 1522). Later seat of Sandzak-Krka Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Surroundings absorbed Vlasi-Uskoplja settlement c. 1528; later receives Vlachs Bjelajaca from Bosnia 1690.
Per Desnica (1646–1684)
Throughout the corpus the operational base of the Krčki sandžak-beg (Durakbegović 1670s–80s), the kapetan (Atlagić, then Firdusović 1680s+), and the disdar (Mehmed-aga). Recurring base of Ottoman counter-raids against the Kotari.

1648-04 — Conquered by Foscolo’s force after Klis (doc. 26); held only briefly.
1653-10-22 — Stojan Janković under Knin’s walls beheads aga Asan Cuna (Grgur Galiotović as alfier; doc. 77).
1666-04-05 — Knin Turks form the chief Ottoman muster behind the Cetina rotta.
1675-08-29 — Mehmed-beg Atlagić’s letter in Bosnian Cyrillic (doc. 214).
1683-12-16 — Pađen battle: 24 Kotarska zastave under Knin’s walls (docs. 353, 355). 10 Turks killed; 3 Kotarci dead/missing (Martin Suskovich da Budin, Bose Sudanović Bužanin, one from Ljuba).
1683 (Christmas) — Turks abandon Knin briefly, return; 1500-strong Ottoman base by Feb 1684 (doc. 384).

People (Ottoman side)

Mehmed-beg Atlagić — kapetan kninski.
Mustaj-beg Firdusović — kapetan kninski 1683 (doc. 380).
Mehmed-aga — disdar.
Asan Cuna — aga, beheaded 1653.
Omer-aga Vidimlić — 1679 (doc. 261).

In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Major fortress, multiple raids and skirmishes 1684–1685 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Mehmed-beg Durakbegović sandžak-beg until early 1685. Sandžak-beg Mehmed Beg Cernicich (sangiacco of Krka, Lika, Krbava); his son Mahmut Beg disdar/castellan of Knin fortress.
Knin Battle 2 June 1684 (doc 9): 2000 Kotari Morlachs under Janković, Smiljanić, Bortulačić; victory; ~120 Turks killed; 90 horses captured; Janković lightly wounded.
Mikiel’s reconnaissance (Feb 1685, doc 51): Mikiel + Janković + Smiljanić, 600-strong; burned Knin’s outlying houses; 4 Turks captured.
Knin Conquest (29 August – 11 September 1688) [docs 213–220]: Cornaro’s 15-day siege; assault Sep 2 (city); siege of inner fortresses; surrender Sep 11 by Atlagić to discretion. First/second recinto; fortress on Grebano; mosque converted to Catholic church; 11 bronze cannons captured; 600+ defenders, 300 perished, 1000 souls left, 150 Venetian subjects in chains freed. Atlagić, his son Mehmed Beg, nephew Alibeg captured. Convoy from Banja-Luka failed to relieve.
Krajina post-conquest: Sinobad governor/sopraintendente; Bulin Most + Aqua Radeglievaz lands; many Turkish houses (Hadži-Kurtović, Hadži-Emorić, Acmet-aga Livaković); Cossovo plain (Kosovo-Polje-Knin) full of new subjects; Juka Vukmirović Morlach habitant. Cadi-grande of Knin oversaw Skradin, Krka river, Strmica, Bošnjake, Komazlić, Golubić, Starčević, Otton, Pađene, Mokro-Polje, Bribir, Ivosenze, Barivode, Radučić, Zegar (doc 315). 1689 conquest details: Bjelajci settled with Pirić in Durakbegović tower; Selman pasha threatened Knin from Mostar.

places/Kolarin.title: Kolarin
places/Kolarin.content:
Kolarina
Village in the Zadar hinterland associated with uskok families in Desnica I Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I.

places/Konjsko.title: Konjsko
places/Konjsko.content:
Konjsko
Campsite near Sinj/Klis; Zeno camped here before joining Cornaro April 1687 (doc 169) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Koper.title: Koper
places/Koper.content:
Koper (Capodistria)
Venetian Istrian seat. Potestat and capitano in 1524: Zuane-Minoto-b????-Venice — captured the Habsburg-subject Tomas-Ruzic-b????-Sibenik over Ottoman dealings Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

places/Korcula.title: Korcula
places/Korcula.content:
Korčula
Adriatic island (doc 55) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Cornaro went here (doc 193). Peri’s origin.

places/Korlat.title: Korlat
places/Korlat.content:
Korlat
Village near Benkovac (1528: “Korlatović” with mezra Tihlić, 5 non-Muslim houses) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Old Catholic churches Sv. Nediljica, Sv. Jere, Uznesenja BDM. Adjacent Tihlić = today’s Kula-Atlagica.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Under Nadin pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga (with Biljane, Sopot, Benkovac, Perušić, Kozulovac, Kula-Atlagica, Cossulovo Polje, Ostrovica) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Zaviša Janković’s holdings (oxen 1699/1700). 300 men under Kalinić from Korlat raided Kanjiža April 1688 (doc 202).

places/Kosinj.title: Kosinj
places/Kosinj.content:
Kosinj
Lika locality. 1691 grant location for the Rukavina family Saric-2008-Bunjevci. 1712 popis: Donji Kosinj parish (Otočac regiment) had Vukelić family presence; Bunjevčevići u Kršu kod Kosinja are documented as Orthodox c. 1700.

places/Kosovo-Polje-Knin.title: Kosovo-Polje-Knin
places/Kosovo-Polje-Knin.content:
Kosovo Polje (kraj Knina)
Dalmatian Kosovo polje near Knin (doc 19, in Soppe Fortezza’s sub-region) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Pianura full of new subjects post-1688 conquest. NOT the Kosovo of Serbia. Vid Petrović “da Cossouo” — Kosovo near Sinj area, not this Knin Kosovo nor Serbian Kosovo.

places/Kosovo-near-Sinj.title: Kosovo-near-Sinj
places/Kosovo-near-Sinj.content:
Kosovo (near Sinj)
Village near Sinj (da Cossouo in the sources); birthplace of Vid Petrović Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Kostajnica.title: Kostajnica
places/Kostajnica.content:
Kostajnica
Bosanska Krajina stronghold; 800 cav + 1500 foot Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Captured by Imperials 1688 (doc 214).

places/Kosulovo-Polje.title: Kosulovo-Polje
places/Kosulovo-Polje.content:
Kožulovo polje
Origin locality of uskok families recorded in Desnica I Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I.

places/Kotor.title: Kotor
places/Kotor.content:
Kotor (Cattaro)
Bay of Kotor naval base and Venetian provveditore headquarters Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 72, 174). Threatened by Skadar Sandžak May 1685 (Grbalj/Zuppa contado at risk). Boka where Laližić was exarch 1695. Levant career station of Ottaviano Lazzari (doc 345).

places/Kozica.title: Kozica
places/Kozica.content:
Kozica
Village under Biokovo in Vrgoračka krajina. 1477 Hercegovina defter: part of the Sladović džemat (with Podaca and Igrane) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

places/Kozino.title: Kozino
places/Kozino.content:
Kožino
Village in Julio Soppe’s sub-region (doc 19); under Zemunik pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
1610 census (Museo Correr) Dundovic-1610-Zadar-Census
23 households, 113 souls (32 men, 37 women, 23 boys and 21 girls). Heads of household:

places/Kozulova-Polje.title: Kozulova-Polje
places/Kozulova-Polje.content:
Kožulova Polje
Most fertile area of the Vilajet Hrvati between Klicevac and Ostrovica fortresses, named after the pre-Ottoman noble Vlach family Kožul (Kožulić) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Endowed as the vakuf of Gazi-Husrev-beg in 1531 (first as čiftluk, later nahija Kožulova). 1574 register lists 97 “Istarska raja” houses across ~20 villages and mezre. Today only the village Kožlovac east of Benkovac preserves the name.

places/Kozulovac.title: Kozulovac
places/Kozulovac.content:
Kožulovac
Mikiel’s tour, 4 miles south of Vrana (doc 51) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Under Nadin pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga (with Biljane, Sopot, Benkovac, Perušić, Korlat, Kula-Atlagica, Cosulovo Polje, Ostrovica). See also Kozulova-Polje (existing) for the polje.

places/Kranjska.title: Kranjska
places/Kranjska.content:
Kranjska (Carniola)
Habsburg duchy. Affected by 1570 peasant unrest (wine tax) extending to Pazinska-Grofovija; site of Pazin-Peasant-Revolt-1570. Includes Bela-Krajina (south) and Notranjska (inner) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

places/Kras.title: Kras
places/Kras.content:
Kras
Karst plateau in the Habsburg-Venetian borderlands above the Adriatic. Major refuge for Croatian Vlachs fleeing Ottoman conquests c. 1518–1523 (Vlach-Migration-to-Istria-1518-1523). Source area of Vlasi-Istre return migration 1528. Includes settlements Vodice-na-Krasu (where Tomas-Ruzic-b????-Sibenik was attested 1524), Buzet, Rašpor Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

places/Krbava.title: Krbava
places/Krbava.content:
Krbava
Karst plateau region, pre-Ottoman seat of the Krbavski princes (Ivan-Karlovic-b????-Krbava). Krbava-Modruš diocese. Ottoman conquest 1522–1527 destroyed the knežstvo; some inhabitants migrated north or were taken in Ottoman raids (3000 captives in 1514) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Mehmed Beg Cernicich was sandžak-beg Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (docs 17, 33, 55). Stojan Janković destroyed the area Aug 1687. Imperial reconquest 1689 from Karlovac under Erbestein. Castles: Komic (Cornich), Bunich (Bunić), Bidach, Curiach (uninhabited per Peri), Coremill (Korenica per footnote), Suignaraz (only millet guard).

places/Krickaci.title: Krickaci
places/Krickaci.content:
Kričaci
Village in the Bukovica associated with uskok families in Desnica I Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I.

places/Krivi-Put.title: Krivi-Put
places/Krivi-Put.content:
Krivi Put
Settlement in the Senjska-Kapetanija hinterland in the Senjska Draga; Habsburg-side Krmpote colony cluster with Sv-Jakov, Ledenice, Senjska-Draga. Subject of the Živjeti na Krivom Putu (2008) zbornik in which Saric-2008-Bunjevci appears.

places/Krk.title: Krk
places/Krk.content:
Krka (Sandžak)
Ottoman sandžak on the Dalmatian frontier (also Sandžak of Cetina). Its sandžak-begs from before 1671 to 1684 were of the Durakbegovic beg family, whose zijamet was at Vrana Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I.
Notes
The bare link [[Krk]] used on some pages refers to this Krka sandžak, not the Adriatic island of Krk. See also Sandzak-Krka and Krka.

places/Krka-Manastir.title: Krka-Manastir
places/Krka-Manastir.content:
Krka (manastir Sv. Arhangela)
Greek-rite (Orthodox) monastery on Krka river, granted to Greek-rite monks 1690 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Bounded by Lačani (vignale), Migliaska (three mills), Karslac (boschetto), Atlum Greb, Biela Vlaha, Giama Colubinca, Skradin road, Zerveni stine od Celine — 100 fields total.

places/Krka.title: Krka
places/Krka.content:
Krka (river)
River; “cadi grande” of Knin oversaw the area (doc 315) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Krka monastery of San Michiel Arcangelo (Sv. Arhangel) granted to Greek-rite monks 1690; bounded by Lačani, Migliaska (three mills), Karslac, Atlum Greb, Biela Vlaha, Giama Colubinca, Skradin road. Šuplja Crkva (Supglacriqua) — ruined church near Krka, on road to Knin (doc 51).

places/Krmcina.title: Krmcina
places/Krmcina.content:
Krmčina
Village in Bortulačić’s sub-region (docs 19, 51) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Under Zaravecchia pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga.

places/Krmpote-Bukovica.title: Krmpote-Bukovica
places/Krmpote-Bukovica.content:
Krmpote (Bukovica)
Village in Bukovica near Zelengrad; distinct from Krmpote-Senj Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 301). 15 houses settled by Mede Milcović 1693; later harassed Parčić. Mede Milicovich capo.
Cross-reference
Three Krmpotes documented in this wiki: (a) Krmpote near Senj (existing), (b) Krmpote-Senj, (c) this Krmpote-Bukovica near Zelengrad.

places/Krmpote-Senj.title: Krmpote-Senj
places/Krmpote-Senj.content:
Krmpote (Senj area)
Habsburg-territory village in the Senjska-Kapetanija, settled by Krmpote families starting in the 1605/1627 migrations from Hercegovinian/Ottoman Krmpote (today Medvidja). Center of the Sv. Jakov parish (Sv-Jakov), with adjacent settlement clusters Krivi-Put, Ledenice, Senjska-Draga Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
Eponymous transfer of the Hercegovinian katun name onto a new homeland — characteristic of Krmpote toponymy throughout the Tromeđa.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Luka Njegovan formerly lived here; brought 40–50 families to Vinjerac in last war Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 186). Distinct from Krmpote-Bukovica (Bukovica village near Zelengrad).

places/Krmpote.title: Krmpote
places/Krmpote.content:
Krmpote (Bukovica)
Ancestral Vlach/Bunjevac district in the Bukovica/Obrovac area (later selo Medvidja), from which the Krmpoćani (Krmpotic) migrated to Habsburg Lic in 1605 and 1627 Saric-2008-Bunjevci. Knez Nikola Tadijić led uskoks “iz Krmpote” at the Battle of Ribnik 1648 Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I.
Notes
The bare link [[Krmpote]] refers to this Bukovica district; see the more specific pages Krmpote-Bukovica and Krmpote-Senj.

places/Krupa.title: Krupa
places/Krupa.content:
Krupa (na Zrmanji)
Village in nahija Zrmanja. 1528–1530: 1 Muslim + 5 non-Muslim houses; residence of Husein-sin-Poropata-b????-Krupa (early Muslim convert) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Later site of orthodox manastir Krupa (Uspenja Bogorodice).
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Krupa monastery decima collected 1704 (doc 355) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Krusevo.title: Krusevo
places/Krusevo.content:
Kruševo (kod Obrovca)
Village in nahija Obrovac (Donja, Gornja Kruševa, with subhamlets Hotišina = Otišina, Ribnice). 1528: ~15 non-Muslim houses Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. 1554 Šibenik record: Vukoslav-Carapotic-b????-Krusevo (likely Krmpotic) and Mate-Milkovic-b????-Krusevo as Ottoman-side debtors. Old Catholic churches Sv. Jure and Sv. Kuzma i Damjan (in Ribnica).
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Under Novigrad pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Mattio Miljanić captain 1704. Inhabitants Đurđević (now Jurjević), Anić, Karamarko, Miljanić, Klanac, Buljat, Marinović still trace into modern Kruševo (per source footnote on 1696 Obrovac inhabitants).

places/Kucista.title: Kucista
places/Kucista.content:
Kućišta
Locality in the Zrmanja area associated with the Najčinović Vlach kindred Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.
People associated with this place

Milic-Jancic-b????-Kucista, Mihovil-Jancic-b????-Kucista, Biljan-Jancic-b????-Kucista, Martin-Jancic-b????-Kucista

places/Kukalj.title: Kukalj
places/Kukalj.content:
Kukalj
Locality on the Venetian side of the Zadar hinterland (novigradski distrikt) where the Frletic Vlach kindred settled in plaćenička military service after the 1538 defection Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

places/Kula-Atlagica.title: Kula-Atlagica
places/Kula-Atlagica.content:
Kula Atlagića
Village near Benkovac. 1528: “Obatija” (= Opatija) with 11 non-Muslim houses; old church Sv. Nikola at “Tihlić”. 1574 vakuf register: paired with Korlat as “Korlatović i Pehlić” (6 Christian houses) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Residence of Fran-Prejic-b????-Opatija (1528).
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Under Nadin pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga (with Biljane, Sopot, Benkovac, Perušić, Kozulovac, Korlat, Cossulovo Polje, Ostrovica) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Atlagić family lands referenced near attacked village.

places/Kupres.title: Kupres
places/Kupres.content:
Kupres
Battle where Ismael pasha defeated Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (Zaviša Janković attestation 1696). Burgo of Glamoč burned by Zaviša after Cuprez.

places/Lantana.title: Lantana
places/Lantana.content:
Lantana
Small islet ~3 miles from Zadar. Outgoing Provveditor Donà was here when Mocenigo arrived May 1684 (doc 1) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Lapac.title: Lapac
places/Lapac.content:
Lapac
Lika locality mentioned in Desnica II Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Ledenice.title: Ledenice
places/Ledenice.content:
Ledenice
Coastal hinterland village on the former Zrinski estate; one of the Krmpote Habsburg-side colony cluster villages alongside Lic, Krmpote-Senj, Krivi-Put, Senjska-Draga Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
In the 1681 Dvorska komora inquiry into Zrinski obligations, Krmpote starešine (Marko-Perpich-b????-Krmpote and Stephanus Duich) testified about earlier Ledenice/Lič/Krmpote duties Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

places/Ledinac.title: Ledinac
places/Ledinac.content:
Ledinac
W. Hercegovina locality; 1477 winter pasture of the Krmpote katun (with Buhovo, Borajna, Veseli-Vstak) Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

places/Lic.title: Lic
places/Lic.content:
Lič
Village in Gorski kotar on the former Zrinski estate of Hreljin. Primary Habsburg-side Bunjevac settlement nucleus in the early 17th c. — destination of two reconstructed Krmpote migration waves:

1605 — first migration: 24+ Krmpote families, 15 Vojnić families, 20 Sladović “Gvozdenovi ljudi”.
1627 — second migration: 16 reconstructed families incl. Pavelic, Starcevic, Vukelic, Tomljanovic, Prpic.

Family lists per Pavličević 1989, medium confidence Saric-2008-Bunjevci. From Lič and the Senj coast, these families further dispersed into Lika (1690+) and Bačka.

places/Licko-Lesce.title: Licko-Lesce
places/Licko-Lesce.content:
Ličko Lešće
Village in the Otočac kapetanija (Lika) into which a Senj branch of the Sladovići later moved Saric-2008-Bunjevci.
People associated with this place

Manojlo-Sladovic-b????-Lika

places/Lika.title: Lika
places/Lika.content:
Lika
Karst plateau region east of Velebit. Pre-Ottoman home of “kraljevski Vlasi” (royal Vlachs); post-conquest part of Ottoman territory with major yaylak pastures (Mazinska planina, Čemernica) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Place of timar holdings for Petar-Prejic-b???? and Culina-sin-Milica-b???? (1528–1530). Toponym “Istrijanska Glavica” near Raduč preserves memory of Vlasi-Istre summer grazing.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Major source of new Morlak immigrants 1684–1685 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 8: 152 families/2300 souls; doc 70: 70 families/900 souls). Lika migration May 1685: Janković brought 70 Lika families (900 souls) under Polo Michiel’s authority. Atlagić wanted to escape Hungarian campaign; raids on Bilaj, Rebac, Udbina. Imperial conquest 1689 from Karlovac under Erbestein. 1731 Lika border cordon difficulties — communication halted. Many fortresses: Bjelaj, Sotkolač, Krug, Ostrosach, Presnić, Trzac, Krekovica, Mutuica, Kurlić, Zudurovo, Peć (Lika), Posmid, Vranograč, Cazin, Bila Stena, Buzim, Sgodagraski, Korica, Pedalj, Mali/Veliki Gračac, Mali/Veliki Obrovac (Lika), Bihać, Pazarišta, Bilai, Grabenec, Široka Kula, Budach, Brlog, Rebac, Perušić, Udbina (300 cav + 800 foot). 1684 Venetian raid burned Medak and other villages.

places/Limska-Draga.title: Limska-Draga
places/Limska-Draga.content:
Limska draga
Karst valley in central Istria, in the area of medieval Dvigrad. 1622 — selo Jural in Limska draga received 14 Orthodox Crnogorac families from Mrkojevici under pop Jovan, and (briefly) 12 Catholic families under fra Franjo Poruba Saric-2008-Bunjevci. The Catholic families separated and complained to rašporski kapetan Contarini.

places/Lipica.title: Lipica
places/Lipica.content:
Lika upper Krajina micro-fortresses
Note placeholder for several Lika fortresses listed in Peri’s relazione Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (Sotkolač, Krug/Kruga, Ostrosach, Presnić, Krekovica, Mutuica, Kurlić, Zudurovo, Peć, Posmid, Vranograč, Bila Stena/Bjela Stijena, Sgodagraski, Korica, Pedalj, Široka Kula, Budach, Brlog/Berlet, Grabenec). Most were minor castles; not pursued individually pending source confirmation.

places/Lisani.title: Lisani
places/Lisani.content:
Lišane
Village in the Zadar hinterland. In 1671 col. Vuk Crnica (Cernizza) received an investitura including land in Tinj, Bubnjane, and Lišane Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I.

places/Lisicic.title: Lisicic
places/Lisicic.content:
Lisičić
Locality (Rusichia Draga) where Grgur Lepur was a pre-war landholder; one of 20 families who lived in Lisičić moved to Perušić during the Morean War Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Livno.title: Livno
places/Livno.content:
Livno
Bosnian frontier town (docs 9, 16, 27, 28, 30, 33, 38, 40, 53, 56, 60–62, 65) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Atlagić based here. Ali pasha of Hercegovina arrived with cavalry 1688. Burned by Zaviša (Klivuc / Cliuz). Bosnian Pasha’s stop March 1685 (doc 53).

places/Ljuba.title: Ljuba
places/Ljuba.content:
Ljuba
Village in Ventura’s sub-region (doc 19); under Posedarje pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Ljubac.title: Ljubac
places/Ljubac.content:
Ljubač
Fortress and locality on the coast between Pag and Zadar. Uskoks from Jesenice in the Velebit Podgorje were settled between Pag and the fortress of Ljubač (1648) Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I; the Dobrići from Dobropoljci were settled in Ljubač in 1648 Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I. Ljubač was also a transit point in the 1538 Vlach transport to Istria Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

places/Ljubusa.title: Ljubusa
places/Ljubusa.content:
Ljubuša
Mountain in W. Hercegovina; 1477 summer pasture of the Krmpote katun (with Cvrsnica and Vran) Saric-2008-Bunjevci. Also documented in 1670–71 visitation by makarski biskup Marijan-Lisnjic-b???? noting “Morlak” pastors and fra Anto-Ripcanin-b????.

places/Ljubuski.title: Ljubuski
places/Ljubuski.content:
Ljubuški
Hercegovina town (docs 7, 55) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. See also Vojnici-Ljubuski (existing).

places/Lovinac.title: Lovinac
places/Lovinac.content:
Lovinac
Lika village; one of three core Bunjevac settlement nuclei (with Pazariste and Smiljan) from 1690 Lika-Bunjevac-Colonization-1690. 1712 župnik: Damjan-Zdunic-b????-Lovinac — the pop Zduna of folk tradition Saric-2008-Bunjevci.

places/Lukovo.title: Lukovo
places/Lukovo.content:
Lukovo
Village 10 Italian miles from Karlobag; the Senj statute extends only to here Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Site of duel between Mesić and Mitrović (doc 364 footnote — likely Saviša Janković).

places/Macarsca.title: Macarsca
places/Macarsca.content:
Makarska
Adriatic town on the Dalmatian coast. In 1663 Mihail Miličević (Mihaljevic) was granted a paga intera di soldato at Makarska Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I.

places/Mahurci.title: Mahurci
places/Mahurci.content:
Mahurci
Village under Nin pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Maidan.title: Maidan
places/Maidan.content:
Maidan
Town/place where Bosnian Pasha gathered troops March 1685 (doc 53) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Makarska.title: Makarska
places/Makarska.content:
Makarska
Adriatic port and Riviera center, Hercegovina relazione (doc 7, 33) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Listed Sept 1687 with Almissa and Poljica for Morlach captain assemblies (doc 177). Receiving area for Ivan Rašić’s group 1692 (200 souls / 25 families settled at Zavojane, Stigli, Hadži Lukovo).

places/Malpaga.title: Malpaga
places/Malpaga.content:
Malpaga
Village south of Zadar near Sukošan/Bibinje, in Smiljanić’s sub-region (docs 19, 51) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Listed under Zemunik pertinenza in 1689 Cornaro Liga.

places/Marcana.title: Marcana
places/Marcana.content:
Marčana
Village in southern Istra settled 1583 by a group of Morlaci Istrijani (Zadar refugees and Morlaks) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

places/Marindol.title: Marindol
places/Marindol.content:
Marindol (kod Črnomlja)
Uskok settlement in Bela-Krajina near Črnomelj. 1551 register of uskoci records Stanoje-Prijic-b????-Marindol as desetnik (among the Prejic kin who moved north from Ottoman territory) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

places/Marok.title: Marok
places/Marok.content:
Márok
Selo in Sandzak-Mohac (mod. Baranya county, Hungary). 1554 defter records rajetin Marton-Bunavac-b????-Marok (“Márton Bunavácz”) — the earliest known written form possibly representing the surname/etnik “Bunjevac” Saric-2008-Bunjevci (caveats noted on the person page).

places/Medak.title: Medak
places/Medak.content:
Medak
Lika village burned by Venetian raid 1684 (doc 316) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Medvedgrad.title: Medvedgrad
places/Medvedgrad.content:
Medvedgrad
Castle near Zagreb, where Ivan Karlović died 1531 Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Medvidja.title: Medvidja
places/Medvidja.content:
Medviđa
Village in Bukovica. 1528–1530: 6 non-Muslim houses, dzemat of Petar-Milovanic-b????-Medvidja (also home of his brother Tomas-Milovanic-b????-Medvidja) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. 1540 register: 5 non-Muslim + 1 Muslim houses. Later “Krmpotsko Selo” hamlet (today Staro Selo) added by Bunjevac Krmpotic settlers; old church Sv. Ivan Krstitelj “Usik”.

places/Miljevci.title: Miljevci
places/Miljevci.content:
Miljevci
Region (group of villages) in the Drniš–Skradin hinterland, associated with the Dragojl family Desnica-1950-Kotarski-Uskoci-I.

places/Milohanic-i.title: Milohanic-i
places/Milohanic-i.content:
Milohanići
Vlach settlement in the Pazin county (Habsburg inner Istria), one of the villages hosting Vlach settlers alongside Tinjan Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre.

places/Miranje.title: Miranje
places/Miranje.content:
Miranje
Village in Ravni-Kotari. Settled 1528 with Jagodnja as the dzemat of Tomas-Ruzic-b????-Sibenik (26 houses, fertile land yielding 1143 akčes) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Donje and Gornje Miranje were also a joint timar of Ivanis-Poropat-b????-Mirko and Ivaniš sin Mirka (2000 akčes split). Later orthodox church of Sv. Mihajlo built on site of medieval Catholic predecessor.

places/Mletacka-Dalmacija.title: Mletacka-Dalmacija
places/Mletacka-Dalmacija.content:
Mletačka Dalmacija (Venetian Dalmatia)
Coastal Dalmatia under Venetian rule: Zadar, Sibenik, Trogir, Split, islands. Reception area for Vlasi-Istre crossing 1538 (~5,000 to Zadar contado, of whom ~1,000+ retained by Antonio-de-Mula-b????-Venice) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Border with Ottoman Klis sandžak unstable until late 16th c.

places/Mletacka-Istra.title: Mletacka-Istra
places/Mletacka-Istra.content:
Mletačka Istra (Venetian Istria)
Coastal and southern Istria under Venetian rule. Designated Scudo della Dominante (“shield of the Dominante”) for its strategic value protecting Venice. Major reception zone for Vlach refugees 1538 — ~2,000 families settled, declining to ~1,700 by 1554 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Settlements include Premantura, Marcana, Zbandalj, Sikici, plus older villages absorbing newcomers.

places/Mljet.title: Mljet
places/Mljet.content:
Mljet
Adriatic island; Cornaro’s galley at Polače in Mljet harbor (doc 176) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.

places/Modrino-Selo.title: Modrino-Selo
places/Modrino-Selo.content:
Modrino selo
Village in Bukovica near St. Peter’s church (doc 302) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Sinobad family ancestors lavorano under Turks here. House of Turco Modre granted to Sinobad 1692; later disputed.

places/Modro-selo.title: Modro-selo
places/Modro-selo.content:
Modro (Modrino selo)
Casale (rural settlement) in Bukovica near the parish church of Sv. Petar.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
The casale and surrounding lands were originally held by a Turk known only as “Modre” (eponym of the place). After 1692 the lands passed to the Sinobad family. In 1697, Radoš Kresović and his brother Sava Kresović took possession of the casale and refused to return it to Sinobad — a recorded land dispute (doc 302) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II.
People associated

“il Turco Modre” — original Ottoman owner
Sinobad family — successor proprietors after 1692
Radoš Kresović and Sava Kresović — 1697 occupiers in dispute

places/Mokro-Polje.title: Mokro-Polje
places/Mokro-Polje.content:
Mokro Polje
Village near Knin. Concentration of Orthodox Vlach population by 1636 Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Settled by Vlachs Bjelajaca from Bosnia 1690.
Per Desnica

1670-08-12 — Barbaro stations a 25-soldier guard there under capt. Marko Grubišić of Novigrad (doc. 174).
1683-12-16 — Kotarci-Šibenčani raid Pađen sub-village; some return through Mokro Polje (doc. 353).
1684-01-11 — Vukadin Bjedov da Mokropoglie (10 houses) settled at Obrovac after the Vrana uprising (doc. 364).
1684-02-28 — 600 minute + 150 grosse animali plundered “christiani sotto Grazaz” by 130 Obrovac Morlachi joined with Novigrađani (doc. 379).

In Desnica II (1684–1749)
Cadi-grande of Knin oversaw Mokropoglie Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II (doc 315). Assigned to Bjelajci 1692 (along with Plavno, Zrmanja, Pađene, Oton). Đuro Popović harambaša 1693. Selman pasha raid ~1696 — Sinobad repulsed; killed 100 Turks, 100 enslaved; nephew killed.

places/Morlakija.title: Morlakija
places/Morlakija.content:
Morlakija
Cartographic-imagological region of the early modern eastern Adriatic hinterland, broadly overlapping with the Tromedja and Velebit Podgorje. Used by Venetian observers (e.g. Vincenzo-Forza-b???? 1636) to designate the Vlach-populated mountainous backlands Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. “Bukovica je jedna od najvećih planina Morlakije” — Forza.

places/Mostar.title: Mostar
places/Mostar.content:
Mostar
Hercegovinian fortress and nahija seat. 1477 istimâlet contracts here brought Vlachs led by Vladimir-vojvoda-b????-Hercegovina back to Mostar/Hum nahija under sandžakbeg Hamza-beg-b???? and vojvoda Sinan-beg-b????-Mostar Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. Mehmed-beg-b????-Poljica (sandžakbeg of Hercegovina, early 16th c.) was a native of Poljica.
In Desnica II (1684–1749)
District descriptions in fra Mijo Radonić’s Hercegovina relazione May 1684 (doc 7) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. District includes Rakitno; raided by Kaštelani / Splićani 1687. Rašić family origin (Rusić village, Mostar district); Selman pasha of Hercegovina threatened Knin. Ilija Janković distinguished himself “sotto Mostar” in Venetian campaign (doc 375).

places/Mrkojevici.title: Mrkojevici
places/Mrkojevici.content:
Mrkojevići
Vlach montenegrin region near Bar in Sandzak-Skadar. In 1622, pop Jovan iz Mrkojevića led 14 Orthodox Crnogorac families to selo Jural in Limska-Draga in Mletacka-Istra. They were accompanied by 12 Catholic families under fra Franjo Poruba — the Catholic group separated, citing “uiuer essi sotto il rito latino, et gli altri sotto il Greco; onde non stariano mai bene insieme” — an early concrete instance of intra-Vlach rite-based separation Saric-2008-Bunjevci (Bertoša 1986:169).

places/Muskovci.title: Muskovci
places/Muskovci.content:
Muškovci
Village near Obrovac — territorialized katun of the medieval Mušković Vlachs (catunar Dien Mušković, 1433 Lika royal-Vlach charter) Saric-2024-Vlasi-Istre. 1544: 25 families from here fled Lika summer pasture into Habsburg Prilisce.

places/Nadin.title: Nadin
places/Nadin.content:
Nadin
Castello (capo di Morlacchi di Nadin: Šimun Bortulačić, doc 10) Desnica-1951-Kotarski-Uskoci-II. Pertinenza HQ from 1689 Cornaro Liga; Zeno’s camp. Pertinenza included Biljane, Sopot, Benkovac, Perušić-Benkovac, Kožulovac, Korlat, Kula-Atlagica, Cosulovo Polje, up to Ostrovica. Cula Smilčić, Pristeg, Boista listed under Nadin.
